Title: MEMORANDUM - Defending the Carbon Pricing Package: Strategic Lines for the Week Ahead

TO: Senior Political Staff
FROM: Communications & Strategy Unit
RE: Offensive and Defensive Messaging for Carbon Pricing Defence

1. BOTTOM LINE
This policy is the most efficient, pro-growth, and fair mechanism to cut emissions, drive clean innovation, and keep our industry competitive in a carbon-constrained global economy. We hold the high ground on economics and fairness; our task this week is to stay on the front foot and reframe the debate from "cost" to "investment and competitiveness."

2. WHY THIS PACKAGE IS THE RIGHT CHOICE
- Economic efficiency: A single, predictable price signal lets businesses decide how to reduce emissions at least cost, avoiding costlier command-and-control regulation.
- Investment certainty: Fixed price paths with legislated trajectories give investors the confidence to finance long-term capital projects in clean technology and energy efficiency.
- Revenue recycling: Returning proceeds to households and targeted industries ensures the system is fair, protects purchasing power, and supports transition investments.
- Global alignment: Major trading partners (EU via CBAM, Canada, UK) are moving to price carbon; our system ensures domestic firms are not caught unprepared or penalized at the border.

3. COMPETITIVENESS, INNOVATION, AND FAIRNESS
- Competitiveness: Output-based pricing and targeted relief for trade-exposed sectors keep our producers on a level playing field while preserving the incentive to improve.
- Innovation dividend: Every dollar of carbon revenue reinvested in R&D, retrofits, and industrial transformation lowers future abatement costs and builds export-ready clean-tech clusters.
- Fairness for households: [X]% of revenue is returned directly to families through [rebates/tax credits], with low-and-middle-income households receiving more than the average cost impact.
- Fairness for workers: The [Just Transition/Worker Transition Fund] channels support into reskilling, community diversification, and early-retirement pathways where needed.

4. ANTICIPATED ATTACKS AND USABLE COUNTERS
Attack: "This is a job-killing tax."
Counter:
- This is not a tax that disappears into general revenue; it is a market mechanism with every dollar recycled back into the economy through household rebates and business investment.
- Independent analysis shows the net employment effect is positive over the medium term, with [sector X] already adding [number] jobs in clean energy and efficiency.
- The real risk to jobs is falling behind trading partners who are decarbonizing their industrial bases and will soon screen our exports at the border.

Attack: "Families can't afford higher energy prices."
Counter:
- The average household receives [rebate amount] annually, which covers and typically exceeds the estimated price impact on fuel and utilities.
- The price signal is modest and predictable—roughly [X cents/litre] at the pump—while efficiency standards and investments help families permanently lower their energy bills.
- Without this plan, we remain exposed to volatile global fossil-fuel markets that have delivered far larger price spikes than any carbon price.

Attack: "We are undermining our own industry while competitors do nothing."
Counter:
- Our trade-exposed sectors receive [output-based allocations/transition support] calibrated to maintain parity.
- The EU and other major markets are implementing carbon border adjustments; our domestic price ensures our exporters will not face tariffs on entry.
- Delaying action forces a steeper, more disruptive retrofit later, stranding assets and ceding the clean-tech market to rivals.

5. MAJOR VULNERABILITIES—BRIEF NOTE
Two timing risks require monitoring: (1) the lag between visible fuel/utility price changes and the arrival of rebate payments in households, creating a temporary perception gap; and (2) any slippage in announced investment timelines for trade-exposed sectors, which opponents will exploit. Mitigating both requires front-loaded communication on rebate schedules and rapid deployment of announced industrial supports.

6. LIFT-READY TALKING POINTS
- "This is a plan for jobs and competitiveness, not a tax grab. Every dollar goes back to families and forward-looking businesses."
- "We can either set the price ourselves and invest the proceeds here, or let Brussels and Beijing set it for us at the border."
- "The choice is not between paying and not paying; it is between paying ourselves and building clean industries, or paying overseas suppliers for volatile fossil fuels."
- "Our rebates ensure that middle-class families are better off, while our industrial safeguards keep production and jobs at home."
- "The companies winning the next century are already investing in low-carbon technology; this package gives everyone else the roadmap and the support to catch up."

CLOSE: The minister should project calm confidence, anchor every answer in household fairness and industrial strategy, and refuse to cede the jobs frame. We have the stronger economic argument; we simply need to keep repeating it with discipline.
